verdicts.trueWording: AI does not and cannot do that work
verdicts.note: Live fetch, HTTP 200. Opening paragraph. The preceding two sentences carry the other limbs: the reputation is built on 'the people who actually go', who walk, eat and ask before judging a hotel - so 'that work' is on-the-ground reporting, and the brand-rests-on-it limb is the reputation sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: We do not use AI to create original editorial reporting
verdicts.note: Section heading 'What we will not do' is on the page verbatim; the sentence continues with recommendations, reviews and destination expertise, so all four items in the claim are listed.

verdicts.trueWording: Eleanor and her husband Theodore Roosevelt
verdicts.note: Live fetch, HTTP 200, no paywall. Slate piece by Nitish Pahwa, November 2025 path. Michael Burgess says he put something about Eleanor Roosevelt into ChatGPT and it returned the phrase; he is a local-history author (self-published local history republished by History Press in 2023). The piece returns to the mix-up in its closing paragraph.

verdicts.trueWording: not going to go and get microfilm
verdicts.note: Same paragraph supplies the remaining limbs: the reporter writes that the book required research Burgess believes AI cannot do, and Burgess names the New York State Library and its microfilm of Franklin Roosevelt's gubernatorial papers. State library limb confirmed.

Live fetch, HTTP 200. Which? press release dated 02 Jul 2026, so 'July 2026' is right. The same sentence names the hotel (Riu Palace Santa Maria, Cape Verde) as the subject of the Tripadvisor AI summary, so the claim's 'that hotel' referent is anchored on the page.

Both limbs sit in one paragraph comparing the platforms for the Britannia International hotel in London: Google's overview is reported as highlighting guest reviews of 'filthy' conditions, and Tripadvisor's summary of the same hotel as praising clean rooms and calling the atmosphere charming.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'opened by saying' - the page never says the passage was the article's opening, and the cited revision shows it was not
verdicts.trueWording: stands as a vibrant town with a rich cultural heritage
verdicts.note: Quotation is verbatim on the page, in section 'Promotional and advertisement-like language' > 'Subtypes', labelled as from a June 2023 revision to Alamata (woreda). I followed the page's own diff link (oldid 1162718043; API confirms timestamp 2023-06-30 and title 'Alamata (woreda)') and fetched the raw wikitext: the lead is a plain one-sentence definition of Alamata as a woreda in Tigray Region, and the 'Nestled within...' passage is the first line of the '== Overview ==' section, not the opening. Puffery limb, June 2023 limb, Ethiopian-woreda limb and the quotation all hold; only the positional limb fails.

verdicts.trueWording: solidify its role as a regional hub
verdicts.note: Same page, section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends' (shortcuts WP:AILEGACY / WP:AITREND), example labelled as from an October 2024 revision to Kumba, Cameroon; the sentence credits road networks connecting Kumba to Mamfe and Buea. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: the text suddenly switches genre, typically inserting a short promotional phrase
verdicts.note: Opening definition sentence; it continues with 'full of sensory details' and 'into an informational text', so the claim's informational-text limb is on the page. Post dated May 13, 2026. Author descriptor on the page is 'Professor and Co-Director of the Center for Digital Narrative at the University of Bergen'; the page never uses the words 'digital culture', so the claim's 'digital-culture professor' is a field paraphrase, not the page's wording.

verdicts.trueWording: a route famous for its scenic views of the mountains and deserts
verdicts.note: Example 2. Surrounding text gives the other limbs: the source is cited as the Government's Memorandum in Support of Pretrial Detention in United States v. Cole Tomas Allen, 29 April 2026, page 9, and the glitch fires on a mention of a long-distance Amtrak passenger train to Chicago. The quoted phrase runs on to 'of the American West'.

verdicts.trueWording: generated an article title in quotations from a specific newspaper
verdicts.note: Live fetch, HTTP 200. Page dated January 9, 2024, by Nikki Koehlert, OHS Reference Librarian. The sentence continues 'on a particular date'. The prompt limb is on the page verbatim as the researcher's ChatGPT prompt about the first Hindu wedding in U.S. media, and the could-not-verify limb is her earlier report that she found neither the article title nor any record of the two named people or such a wedding.

verdicts.trueWording: it found a repeated pattern and produced a conclusion
verdicts.note: Same paragraph carries the mechanism limb: the names and the words wedding/Hindoo appeared on the same Daily Astorian pages in the 1910s but were unrelated, and the sentence closes with the conclusion not being based in fact.

verdicts.trueWording: such books still tend to be full of inaccuracies
verdicts.note: Live fetch, HTTP 200. Governing, published October 3, 2025, by Jule Pattison-Gordon. The phrase is the reporter's own parenthetical inside her sentence about AI writing nonfiction by compiling information available on the Internet, so both the compiled-from-the-internet limb and the reporter-states limb hold.

verdicts.trueWording: confidently written and full of vivid adjectives
verdicts.note: Live fetch, HTTP 200. Gongora Meza is described as founder and director of Evolution Treks Peru, overhearing tourists planning a hike to the 'Sacred Canyon of Humantay', and he states there is no such place. The thing he describes is 'the screenshot'; the article's own framing (travellers using AI to create itineraries; a program like ChatGPT) supports calling it an AI itinerary. Metadata caveat: URL slug is 20250926 but the live page displays 29 September 2025; the claim sentence asserts no date, so the grade is unaffected.

verdicts.trueWording: The name is a combination of two places that have no relation
verdicts.note: Same quoted paragraph; the sentence ends by saying the two places have no relation to the description, which is the claim's 'attached to it' limb. Same date caveat as 1192 (page displays 29 September 2025).
